content: {"rule": "K-S2", "applies": "yes", "applies_why": "The judge text treats lack of explicit textual resolution as a reason for UNDERDETERMINED, which is what K-S2 addresses.", "verdict": "BREACH", "quote": "UNDERDETERMINED -- answered in [CR2] section A.1-2 and [CR3] Link 6 premises 1-3, where descent according to the flesh is weighed against conception of the Holy Ghost without explicit textual resolution of paternity.", "rule_words": "That a single verse does not state a link or its contrary is never a ground for STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED, for either side. When one verse's words carry two meanings at once, both stand; the verse is not open.", "room": "'a single verse does not state a link or its contrary' — (1) the bar applies only when a judge expressly says one verse is silent, so this broader lack-of-resolution reason is allowed; (2) the bar applies to any UNDERDETERMINED resting on non-explicit textual resolution. I read it as (2).", "why": "K-S2 forbids using a verse's not stating a link or its contrary as a ground for UNDERDETERMINED, and the judge's reason is lack of explicit textual resolution of paternity."}
